prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the scene is a compact kitchen with a person initially about 1.5–2 m in front of the camera wearer, while the cooker, counter, rice cooker, refrigerator, and cabinets occupy the nearer right and rear surfaces. The person turns from facing the camera wearer to a side-on orientation and moves right toward the counter, ending roughly 0.7–1.2 m from the camera and within arm’s reach of the counter and rice cooker; the camera wearer’s hand also enters the lower foreground in the third frame at well under 0.5 m. The map makes foreground–background layering and the person’s changing distance more explicit than RGB, including partial occlusion of the counter by the person and objects cut off at the frame edges. Absolute distances are uncertain, and several bright regions—especially walls, cabinets, appliances, and the person in later frames—appear merged or inconsistently scaled, so brightness is more reliable for relative depth within a frame than for comparison across frames.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation isolates the standing person in the first three frames and again as a large, close foreground mask in the fourth, while also identifying portions of the refrigerator, chair, microwave, and a handbag; the fifth frame retains only a microwave mask. It shows the person initially near the center-left facing approximately toward the camera wearer, then becoming side-on and shifting right toward the appliances, with the enlarged fourth-frame mask indicating closer proximity and occlusion of the counter area. The labeled object masks clarify which visible regions are separate instances, but they do not provide metric distance; using RGB and mask size, the person is roughly 1.5–2 m away initially and about 0.7–1.2 m away later, while the labeled appliances are roughly 1–2.5 m away and generally within about 0.5–1 m of the person near the counter. The map is unreliable or incomplete because many major surfaces and objects are unlabeled, the first-frame extra person fragment at the lower-left appears spurious or out of view, the microwave labels jump between different image regions, and the person disappears entirely in the fifth frame despite remaining partly visible in RGB.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides a body skeleton and both hand locations in the first frame, showing a person about 1.5–2 m ahead, upright and facing roughly toward the camera wearer, with raised hands spread to either side at about chest-to-shoulder height. In the second frame the body remains frontal or slightly turned, the hands move closer to the torso, and the person remains beyond the camera wearer’s immediate arm’s reach, although their own hands are close to their body and near the handbag/counter region seen in RGB. This representation makes limb orientation, hand height, and changes in stance clearer than RGB, including which hand joints overlap or are partly hidden. It is unreliable after the second frame because no skeleton is drawn for frames three through five, and even in the first two frames several head and hand keypoints cluster above or around the body, indicating uncertain localization and preventing a dependable judgment of gaze direction beyond coarse head/body orientation.
